bibliographic.title: Perspective LLM potentiality and awareness: a position paper from the perspective of trustworthy and responsible AI modeling
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sarker, I. H. (2024). Perspective LLM potentiality and awareness: a position paper from the perspective of trustworthy and responsible AI modeling. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 4, 40. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-024-00129-0

methodology.technology_context: Large language models (LLMs), GPT, BERT, chatbots, virtual assistants, NLP, deep learning

eligibility.decision_rationale: Position paper explicitly on LLM potentiality, risks, and trustworthy/responsible AI themes including fairness, transparency, explainability, trust, and accountability; mentions chatbots and virtual assistants and domains such as finance and healthcare, but does not center conversational governance mechanisms in regulated deployments.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction were provided; full-text sections on applications, governance mechanisms, and regulated-context operational controls were not available for verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal adapted to a non-empirical position paper. Objective and scope are clearly stated, but empirical sampling, data collection, and explicit limitations cannot be assessed from the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent and clearly framed around trustworthy and responsible LLM use, but available text is limited to abstract and introduction, the work is conceptual rather than empirically grounded, and conversational governance in regulated operational settings is only indirectly addressed.

coding.theme: Trustworthy and responsible AI for large language models
coding.subtheme: LLM risks, awareness, and governance-oriented principles

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs offer major potential across domains but raise substantial trustworthiness, ethical, and societal risks that require awareness and responsible deployment emphasizing fairness, transparency, explainability, trust, and accountability.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a conceptual framing of LLM potentiality and risk awareness from a trustworthy and responsible AI perspective, identifies technical and ethical challenges, and outlines research directions.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting conceptual evidence on trustworthy/responsible LLM governance themes and general risk factors; not sufficient as central evidence for conversational governance mechanisms in regulated LLM systems because chatbots are only briefly mentioned and operational controls such as guardrails, observability, audit, or human oversight are not evidenced in the provided text.
